newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel steady, but trade thins out.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel steady, but trade thins out.

text.p: European straight-run fuel prices were steady on Thursday, in line with crude, with physical business thin after the spate of deals earlier in the week, traders said.
Offers were believed to be around $106-$107 a tonne fob while bids were heard at $104. Supply was limited though two end-month cargoes were believed available.

Baltic Sea Russian cargoes were again scarce. However Black sea Russian straight-run was amply offered, with M-40s being picked up and eastern Mediterranean bunker demand met by inland waterway barges.
"There are a lot of Volganaft (barges) coming through. It's the real beginning of the river business," said one trader.
